data.title: Roxithromycin
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antibacterials_

**Class:** Semisynthetic 14-membered macrolide

## Mechanism of action
- 50S ribosomal inhibitor (like erythromycin); acid-stable

## Pharmacokinetics
- Better absorbed and longer acting than erythromycin (half-life about 12 h); less CYP3A4 inhibition

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Skin and soft-tissue infections, impetigo, folliculitis in penicillin allergy
- Acne (alternative), NGU/chlamydia (older regimens)

## Dose & formulations
- 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg once daily before food; children 5–8 mg/kg/day

## Adverse effects
- GI upset (less than erythromycin), rash, raised LFT, QT prolongation (rare)

## Contraindications
- Macrolide allergy; with ergot alkaloids

## Drug interactions
- Weaker CYP3A4 inhibition than erythromycin; caution with QT drugs, theophylline, warfarin

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data; erythromycin or azithromycin preferred.

## Viva points
- Acid-stable erythromycin analogue with twice-daily dosing and fewer GI effects

_Sources: Khopkar ch.1 (Roxithromycin, Table 1.7); Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
